story_type: shipboard laser weapon destroys boat targets and a drone
hook: A beam of light set off the explosives on this boat.
narration: Explosives were strapped to this target boat. A laser on a Navy ship set them off.
In 2014, USS Ponce took the Navy's first working laser weapon into the Persian Gulf.
For three months, sailors aimed it at small boats racing toward the ship.
There is no shell. The beam heats one spot until it burns through.
The operators steered it with a controller built like a video game.
Each shot cost less than a dollar. A missile for the same job can cost millions.
[short pause] Then they turned it on a Scan Eagle drone flying overhead.
outcome: The laser shot the drone out of the sky, and sailors said the weapon worked flawlessly.
title: Navy laser blows up a target boat
description:
In 2014 the Laser Weapon System aboard USS Ponce destroyed explosives on speeding target boats and shot a Scan Eagle drone out of the sky during its first deployment in the Persian Gulf.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by John F. Williams, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/421202/laser-weapon-system-laws
